an organisation that acts for others

latinEntries.meaning: the office or activity of an agent

definition_zh: 侵略；攻击行为；好斗情绪；挑衅言行
definition_en: the act of attacking or invading, or a hostile feeling or behaviour directed at others
core_image: 一个人迈步向前逼近，把对方一路逼退到墙角
scene: 球场上两名球员额头几乎顶在一起，裁判快步插到两人中间。The referee warned both players about their aggression towards each other.
sceneCN: 这里 aggression 是「攻击性、好斗情绪」（第 2 个义项：对他人表现出的敌意行为）；句意为裁判警告两名球员不要互相攻击。图中可辨识物件：球场、哨子、黄色卡片。

pos.zh: 名词：侵略；攻击行为；好斗情绪；挑衅言行

derivatives.zh: 由本词反向构词而来，义为「攻击；侵犯」，较为少用
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「好斗的；积极进取的」
由本词换名词后缀构成，义为「侵略者；挑衅者」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「咄咄逼人地；强势地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「攻击性；好斗」

senses.title: An armed attack by one state on another
senses.definition: the act of one country attacking another without provocation
senses.definitionCN: 一国无端对他国发动的武装攻击
senses.example: The tribunal condemned the invasion as unprovoked aggression.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭谴责这次入侵是毫无缘由的侵略。
senses.why: The word was coined in the seventeenth century precisely for wars of this kind, so the state-against-state sense is its oldest and most legal one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词正是十七世纪为这类战争而造，所以「国对国」是它最古老、也最具法律意味的义项。

senses.title: Hostile feeling and behaviour
senses.definition: hostile or violent feelings and behaviour directed at other people
senses.definitionCN: 指向他人的敌意或暴力情绪与行为
senses.example: Frustration often shows up as aggression in young children.
senses.exampleCN: 挫败感在幼儿身上常常表现为攻击性。
senses.why: Psychology took the same word and moved it inside a person: the attack no longer needs a border, only a target.
senses.whyCN: 心理学沿用了这个词，却把它搬进人的内部：攻击不再需要国界，只需要一个对象。

senses.title: An unprovoked attack in words or actions
senses.definition: an unprovoked attack on a person's rights, dignity, or position, whether by words or by deeds
senses.definitionCN: 对他人权利、尊严或地位的无端侵犯，可以是言语也可以是行动
senses.example: Shouting down a colleague in a meeting counts as verbal aggression.
senses.exampleCN: 在会上把同事吼得说不出话，算是一种言语攻击。
senses.why: Once the target can be a person's dignity rather than a country, any unprovoked push against someone qualifies as aggression.
senses.whyCN: 一旦对象可以是人的尊严而不是国家，任何无端的逼迫都可以算作 aggression。

intro.en: Aggression is built from ad- 'towards' and gradi 'to step', so its core picture is stepping towards someone in a hostile way.
intro.cn: aggression 由 ad-「朝向」与 gradi「迈步」构成，核心画面是带着敌意朝某人迈过去。

items.en: Gradi meant 'to step, walk', and it also underlies gradient and graduate.
items.cn: gradi 意为「迈步、行走」，gradient、graduate 也出自这个词。

items.en: Adding ad- 'towards' produced aggredi, 'to step towards, approach', and then 'to attack'.
items.cn: 加上表示「朝向」的 ad- 得到 aggredi，意为「朝……迈步、接近」，再引申为「攻击」。

items.en: The noun aggressio named the act of attacking; the double g comes from ad- assimilating to the following g.
items.cn: 名词 aggressio 指攻击行为；双写的 g 来自 ad- 向后接 g 的同化。

items.en: French carried the word into diplomatic and military writing before English took it up.
items.cn: 法语先把这个词带进外交与军事文书，英语随后借入。

items.en: English uses aggression first for an unprovoked attack, especially by one state on another.
items.cn: 英语最初用 aggression 指无端的攻击，尤其是国家对国家的侵犯。

items.en: Psychology extended it to individual hostility in the twentieth century, and the everyday sense followed.
items.cn: 二十世纪心理学把它扩展到个人的敌意，日常义随后普及。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin and English words built on gradi; the near-meaning group gathers hostile acts of different scale.
note.cn: 形近组收 gradi 这一词族在拉丁语与英语中的成员；近义组收规模不同的敌对行为。

entries.definition: To attack or begin a quarrel, a rare verb back-formed from aggression.
entries.definitionCN: 发动攻击或挑起争端，是由 aggression 逆构的罕见动词。

entries.definition: The person or country that attacks first.
entries.definitionCN: 首先发动攻击的人或国家。

entries.definition: Ready to attack, or very forceful in pursuing a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 随时准备攻击的，或为达目标而强硬推进的。

entries.definition: Unfriendly or antagonistic feeling, often shown openly.
entries.definitionCN: 不友好或对抗的情绪，常公开表露。

entries.definition: The entry of an army into a country in order to conquer it.
entries.definitionCN: 军队进入他国以图征服。

entries.definition: A violent physical or legal attack on a person.
entries.definitionCN: 对人身的暴力攻击，或法律上的侵犯。

normalIntro.en: Four real parts carry the word: ad-, gradi, the assimilated g, and the noun ending -ion.
normalIntro.cn: 四个真实部件承载这个词：ad-、gradi、被同化的 g，以及名词词尾 -ion。

normal.en: Aggression is ad- plus gradi: stepping towards someone, and the step turns into an attack.
normal.cn: aggression 是 ad- 加 gradi：朝某人迈一步，这一步变成了攻击。

normal.en: The double g records a small accident of Latin spelling: ad- bent into the g that followed.
normal.cn: 双写的 g 记下了一个拉丁拼写的小事故：ad- 被后面的 g 同化了。

normal.en: Aggression, aggressive and aggressor all sit on the same stepping root.
normal.cn: aggression、aggressive、aggressor 都立在同一个「迈步」词根上。

normal.en: Think of a border crossed by an army: that is aggression at its largest.
normal.cn: 想一支越过边界的军队：那是最大尺度上的 aggression。

normal.en: The ending -ion marks a noun of action, so aggression is the act, not the feeling alone.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ion 表示行为名词，所以 aggression 指的是行为本身，而不只是情绪。

abstract.en: Every aggression begins with a step towards someone, which is why proximity is part of the idea.
abstract.cn: 每一次侵犯都始于朝某人迈出的一步，所以「逼近」本身就是这个概念的一部分。

abstract.en: The same word covers armies and tempers because both refuse the other side's boundary.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指军队也指脾气，因为两者都不承认对方的边界。

abstract.en: Naming aggression is already a judgement: it says the first move was unprovoked.
abstract.cn: 把行为称为 aggression 已经是一种判断：它认定那第一步是无端挑起的。

examples.en: The resolution called the border crossing an act of aggression.
examples.cn: 决议把这次越境称为侵略行为。

examples.en: Teachers are trained to spot aggression before it turns physical.
examples.cn: 教师受过训练，要在攻击性演变成动手之前识别出来。

examples.en: His aggression in the debate cost him the support of undecided voters.
examples.cn: 他在辩论中的咄咄逼人让他失去了摇摆选民的支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额个雷神」——额，那个雷神一迈步就撞过来，满身攻击性。

root: 源自拉丁语 aggredi「朝……迈步、进攻」，由 ad-「朝向」与 gradi「迈步」构成，名词 aggressio 即「攻击行为」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses keep the same picture of stepping at someone: a state steps over a border, a person's temper steps at another person, and words step on someone's dignity.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项保留同一个「朝人迈步」的画面：国家越过边界，情绪扑向他人，言语则踩上别人的尊严。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure steps forward, closing the distance, and the other person backs into a corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人向前迈步、缩短距离，另一个人被逼得退向墙角。

branches.en: an army crossing a border at dawn
branches.cn: 拂晓时越过边界的军队

branches.en: a child hitting out when frustrated
branches.cn: 受挫时挥拳的孩子

branches.en: a voice raised until a colleague stops speaking
branches.cn: 把同事吼到不敢开口的那个嗓门

branches.en: a legal verdict that names the first mover
branches.cn: 指出谁先动手的法律裁决

branches.en: one stepping root, from borders to bedrooms
branches.cn: 同一个迈步词根，从国界一直走到家里

intro.en: A prefix of direction, a Latin verb of stepping, and the endings that make the noun and its family.
intro.cn: 一个方向前缀、一个表示「迈步」的拉丁动词，以及构成名词及其词族的词尾。

latinIntro.en: gradi and aggressio are recorded Latin; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: gradi 与 aggressio 都是有文献记录的拉丁词，更早的印欧词根属重构。

definition_zh: 好斗的；有攻击性的；积极进取的；强烈的；侵袭性的
definition_en: ready to attack or argue, very forceful in pursuing goals, or severe enough to be damaging
core_image: 一头低头前冲的公牛，不看两边，只朝目标顶过去
scene: 销售部的白板上写满了数字，经理把马克笔往桌上一拍。The new sales director is aggressive, and she expects the same from her team.
sceneCN: 这里 aggressive 是「积极进取、有闯劲」（第 2 个义项：在目标面前强硬推进、不肯退让）；句意为新销售总监很有闯劲，也要求团队如此。图中可辨识物件：白板、马克笔、图表。

pos.zh: 形容词：好斗的；有攻击性的；积极进取的；强烈的；侵袭性的

derivatives.zh: 由本词同源名词构成，义为「侵略；攻击行为」
由同一词根加名词后缀构成，义为「侵略者；挑衅者」
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「咄咄逼人地；强势地」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「攻击性；好斗」
由本词族逆构的动词，义为「攻击；侵犯」，较为少用

senses.title: Ready to attack or fight
senses.definition: ready to attack, fight, or argue, and likely to do so at small provocation
senses.definitionCN: 随时准备攻击、打斗或争吵，一点刺激就会发作
senses.example: The dog becomes aggressive whenever strangers come near its food.
senses.exampleCN: 一有陌生人靠近它的食物，这条狗就变得凶起来。
senses.why: This is the adjective's oldest layer: a person or animal whose first response to a threat is to step forward rather than back away.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个形容词最古老的一层：面对威胁时，人或动物的第一反应是上前一步，而不是退开。

senses.title: Forceful in pursuit of success
senses.definition: very determined and forceful in pursuing goals, especially in business or sport
senses.definitionCN: 为实现目标而十分坚定、强硬，尤用于商业或体育
senses.example: They took an aggressive approach to winning new customers.
senses.exampleCN: 他们采取了强势的做法去争取新客户。
senses.why: Business took the same forward push and removed the hostility: the energy is kept, the enemy is replaced by a target.
senses.whyCN: 商业沿用了同一个「向前顶」的动作，却去掉了敌意：劲头还在，敌人换成了目标。

senses.title: Unusually strong in method
senses.definition: unusually strong or severe in method, often used when a quick result matters more than caution
senses.definitionCN: 手段上异常强烈或猛烈，通常用于求快而不惜冒险的场合
senses.example: Doctors chose aggressive treatment because the tumour was growing fast.
senses.exampleCN: 因为肿瘤长得很快，医生选择了激进的治疗方案。
senses.why: Here the force is turned on a problem rather than a person, so the word means intense method rather than ill will.
senses.whyCN: 这里的力量是对着问题使的，不是对着人，所以这个词指的是手段猛烈，而非心怀恶意。

senses.title: Spreading fast, of a disease
senses.definition: of a disease, spreading quickly and hard to control
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病扩散迅速、难以控制
senses.example: This is an aggressive form of cancer that needs immediate surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一种侵袭性很强的癌症，需要立刻手术。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word for a growth that behaves like an attacker: it advances quickly and will not be held back.
senses.whyCN: 医学借这个词形容一种像入侵者那样行事的病变：推进快，而且拦不住。

intro.en: Aggressive is the adjective of the same Latin family as aggression: stepping towards someone with force.
intro.cn: aggressive 与 aggression 同属一个拉丁词族，本义是带着力量朝某人迈过去。

items.en: Gradi meant 'to step, walk', the base of a small family that includes gradient and graduate.
items.cn: gradi 意为「迈步、行走」，是包含 gradient、graduate 的小词族的根基。

items.en: ad- 'towards' plus gradi gave aggredi, 'to step towards', and in military use 'to attack'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 gradi 构成 aggredi，意为「朝……迈步」，军事用法中即「进攻」。

items.en: The late Latin adjective aggressivus described someone inclined to attack; it is recorded mainly in glosses.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语形容词 aggressivus 形容倾向于攻击的人，主要见于词表与注释。

items.en: English adopted aggressive first in the plain hostile sense, applied to persons and to states.
items.cn: 英语最初以直白的敌对义采用 aggressive，用于人与国家。

items.en: The business sense of 'forceful, go-getting' is a twentieth-century development, and the medical sense followed.
items.cn: 「强势、有闯劲」的商业义是二十世纪的发展，医学义随后出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the rest of the gradi family; the near-meaning group gathers words for force, each with a different target.
note.cn: 形近组收 gradi 词族的其余成员；近义组收表示「强硬」的词，区别在于力量对着什么使。

entries.definition: The noun for an attack or hostile behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 表示攻击行为或敌意的名词。

entries.definition: The one who attacks first.
entries.definitionCN: 先发动攻击的一方。

entries.definition: The rare verb meaning to attack.
entries.definitionCN: 罕见的动词，意为攻击。

entries.definition: Unfriendly and ready to oppose, but not necessarily violent.
entries.definitionCN: 不友好、随时准备对抗，但不一定动手。

entries.definition: Strong and confident in making a point or pushing a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 表达观点或推行计划时有力而自信。

entries.definition: Standing up for oneself calmly, without attacking others.
entries.definitionCN: 平静地维护自己，而不攻击他人。

normalIntro.en: Four real parts carry the word: ad-, gradi, the assimilated g, and the adjective ending -ive.
normalIntro.cn: 四个真实部件承载这个词：ad-、gradi、被同化的 g，以及形容词词尾 -ive。

normal.en: Aggressive keeps the stepping root of aggression and adds -ive, so it means tending to step at people.
normal.cn: aggressive 保留 aggression 的「迈步」词根，加上 -ive，意为「动不动就朝人迈步」。

normal.en: A bull lowers its head and goes straight: that is the picture behind the word.
normal.cn: 公牛低下头、直直冲过去——这就是这个词背后的画面。

normal.en: The same energy is praise in sales and blame in traffic: context decides whether the force is admired.
normal.cn: 同一股劲头，在销售里是褒，在交通里是贬；是正是邪由语境决定。

normal.en: Aggressive does not take -er: use more and most before it.
normal.cn: aggressive 不加 -er：比较级和最高级用 more 与 most。

normal.en: Note the double g and the single s: ag-gress-ive.
normal.cn: 注意双 g 与单 s：ag-gress-ive。

abstract.en: Force is neutral until we ask who it is aimed at: at a person it is aggression, at a goal it is drive.
abstract.cn: 力量本身是中性的，要问它对着谁：对着人是攻击性，对着目标是闯劲。

abstract.en: A word that can praise and condemn at once shows how much of meaning is carried by context rather than by the root.
abstract.cn: 一个词能同时用来夸奖和指责，说明意义有多少是由语境而非词根承担的。

abstract.en: Calling a disease aggressive grants it a will, because the word was built for creatures that choose to advance.
abstract.cn: 把疾病称作 aggressive，等于赋予它意志，因为这个词本是为会主动进攻的生灵而造的。

examples.en: Some birds become aggressive when their nests are approached.
examples.cn: 有些鸟在巢被人靠近时会变得凶猛。

examples.en: The firm's aggressive pricing forced smaller rivals out of the market.
examples.cn: 这家公司的激进定价把较小的对手挤出了市场。

examples.en: She was aggressive in the interview but never rude.
examples.cn: 她在面试中很有冲劲，但从不失礼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额个雷死我」——额，那个冲过来的家伙差点把我撞死，太有攻击性了。

root: 源自拉丁语 aggredi「朝……迈步、进攻」，由 ad-「朝向」与 gradi「迈步」构成，加形容词后缀 -ive 表示「倾向于」如此。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses share one forward push: at a person it is hostility, at a target it is drive, at a problem it is intense method, and in a body it is a fast-spreading growth.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项共用同一个「向前顶」：对着人是敌意，对着目标是闯劲，对着难题是猛药，对着身体则是扩散很快的病变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bull lowers its head and drives straight ahead, seeing nothing on either side.
core.cn: 核心意象：公牛低下头，直直向前顶，两边什么也看不见。

branches.en: a dog that lunges at anyone near its bowl
branches.cn: 谁靠近食盆就扑上去的狗

branches.en: a sales team that calls first and calls again
branches.cn: 先打电话、再打第二次的销售团队

branches.en: a course of treatment stronger than usual
branches.cn: 比常规更猛的一轮治疗

branches.en: a tumour that spreads before it is found
branches.cn: 还没被发现就已经扩散的肿瘤

branches.en: one pushing force, blamed or praised by its target
branches.cn: 同一股向前的力，因对象不同而被贬或被褒

intro.en: A Latin verb of stepping, the prefix that aims it, and the adjective endings that build the family.
intro.cn: 一个表示「迈步」的拉丁动词、给它定方向的前缀，以及构成这一词族的形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: gradi and aggressivus are recorded Latin; only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: gradi 与 aggressivus 都是有文献记录的拉丁词，只有更早的印欧词根属重构。

definition_zh: 以前；……之前；很久以前
definition_en: before the present time, used after a period of time to say how far back something happened
core_image: 手指从今天这一点往回滑，停在过去的某一格上
scene: 老人坐在门口翻一本旧相册，手指停在某张照片上。She left the village three years ago.
sceneCN: 这里 ago 是「（从此刻往回数的）以前」（第 1 个义项：与时间段连用，表示距现在多久之前）；句意为她三年前离开了这个村子。图中可辨识物件：旧相册、木门、藤椅。

pos.zh: 副词：以前；……之前（置于时间段之后）

derivatives.zh: ago 的古旧变体，见于诗歌与方言，义为「以前」
由 long 与 ago 合成的形容词，义为「很久以前的」

senses.title: Before now, by a stated amount
senses.definition: before the present time, placed after a period of time to state how far back an event happened
senses.definitionCN: 在现在之前，放在时间段之后，说明事情发生在多久以前
senses.example: She left the village three years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 她三年前离开了这个村子。
senses.why: Ago began as the past participle of the old verb 'to go', so 'three years ago' once meant 'three years gone', counted back from today.
senses.whyCN: ago 原本是古英语动词「走」的过去分词，所以「three years ago」早先的意思是「三年已经过去」，是从今天往回数。

senses.title: In the distant past, unmeasured
senses.titleCN: 很久以前（不给出具体距离）
senses.definition: in the fixed phrases long ago and ages ago, at a time far in the past without a stated distance
senses.definitionCN: 用于 long ago、ages ago 等固定说法，指遥远的过去，不说明具体相隔多久
senses.example: Long ago, this valley was covered by a lake.
senses.exampleCN: 很久以前，这条山谷被一个湖覆盖着。
senses.why: Once the measured use was fixed, ago could also carry an unmeasured distance, and long or ages supplies the vagueness on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 表示确切距离的用法固定下来之后，ago 也能承担模糊的距离，由 long 或 ages 故意把这种模糊说出来。

intro.en: Ago is a worn-down past participle of an Old English verb meaning 'to go', and it has kept that backward glance ever since.
intro.cn: ago 是古英语中意为「走」的动词的过去分词，磨损之后留下「已经走过」的回望意味。

items.en: Gan meant 'to go', the ancestor of modern go, and it formed compounds with prefixes of direction.
items.cn: gān 意为「走」，是现代 go 的祖先，能与方向前缀构成复合词。

items.en: Agan, from a- 'away' plus gan 'go', meant 'to go away, pass by', and its participle meant 'gone, passed'.
items.cn: āgān 由 ā-「离开」加 gān「走」构成，意为「走开、过去」，其分词意为「已过去的」。

items.en: The participle shrank to ago and came to be used after a length of time: 'long ago' is literally 'long gone'.
items.cn: 分词缩略为 ago，并开始放在时间段之后使用：long ago 字面上就是「早已过去很久」。

items.en: The modern pattern with a measure, as in 'three years ago', is established in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 「three years ago」这种带计量成分的现代用法，在十四世纪已经确立。

items.en: The old variant agone survives only in poetry and dialect, while ago has become a fixed postposed adverb.
items.cn: 旧变体 agone 只留在诗歌与方言里，而 ago 已成为固定的后置副词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that resemble ago in form; the near-meaning group gathers ways of pointing backwards in time.
note.cn: 形近组收外形与 ago 相近的词；近义组收各种指向过去的时间说法。

entries.definition: An old or dialectal form of ago, now found mainly in verse.
entries.definitionCN: ago 的古旧或方言形式，如今主要见于诗歌。

entries.definition: Very eager or excited to see or hear something.
entries.definitionCN: 急切想看或想听的；兴致勃勃的。

entries.definition: An archaic adverb meaning in motion or in progress.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧副词，意为「在运动中」或「在进行中」。

entries.definition: At an earlier time, often mentioned in a formal report.
entries.definitionCN: 在较早的时候，常用于正式叙述。

entries.definition: At a point before the one being talked about, not necessarily before now.
entries.definitionCN: 在所谈的那个时点之前，不一定是在现在之前。

entries.definition: In the phrase three years back, an informal equivalent of ago.
entries.definitionCN: 用于 three years back 这类说法，是 ago 的口语替代。

normalIntro.en: Two real pieces carry the word: an Old English verb of going and the participle ending worn away.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：一个表示「走」的古英语动词，以及被磨掉的过去分词词尾。

normal.en: Ago is the old participle of go: three years ago means three years gone.
normal.cn: ago 是 go 的古老分词：three years ago 就是「三年已经过去」。

normal.en: It always follows the time, never leads it: two days ago, not ago two days.
normal.cn: 它永远跟在时间后面，不放在前面：说 two days ago，不说 ago two days。

normal.en: Ago measures back from now; before can measure back from any point in the story.
normal.cn: ago 从此刻往回量；before 可以从叙述中的任何一个时点往回量。

normal.en: Long ago and ages ago drop the number and keep only the distance.
normal.cn: long ago 与 ages ago 丢掉数字，只留下距离感。

normal.en: Three letters, and the last is a vowel: a-g-o, unlike the verb go.
normal.cn: 三个字母，最后一个是元音：a-g-o，与动词 go 的拼写不同。

abstract.en: A word for the past built from a verb for walking shows how time is spoken of as movement.
abstract.cn: 用「走」的动词来造表示过去的词，说明人习惯把时间说成运动。

abstract.en: Ago needs a number to be precise and needs long to be vague, so it is a word that borrows its measure from its neighbours.
abstract.cn: ago 要有数字才精确，要有 long 才模糊，它是一个从邻居那里借来尺度的词。

abstract.en: Every use of ago quietly marks a speaker standing at now, looking back.
abstract.cn: 每一次用 ago，都在悄悄标出说话人正站在「现在」这一点上往回看。

examples.en: She left the village three years ago.
examples.cn: 她三年前离开了这个村子。

examples.en: Long ago, this valley was covered by a lake.
examples.cn: 很久以前，这条山谷被一个湖覆盖着。

examples.en: The letter arrived a week ago, but nobody opened it.
examples.cn: 那封信一周前就到了，但没人拆开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额够」——额，够了够了，那都是很久以前的事了。

root: 源自古英语 āgān「走开、过去」，由 ā-「离开」与 gān「走」构成，其过去分词义为「已过去的」，后固定为表示「以前」的副词。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses look backwards from now: one measures the distance with a number, the other leaves the distance deliberately vague.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都从此刻往回看：一个用数字量出距离，另一个故意把距离留在模糊里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger slides back along a timeline and stops on an earlier square.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指沿时间线往回滑，停在前面的某一格上。

branches.en: a calendar page turned back three years
branches.cn: 往回翻三年的日历

branches.en: a letter dated a week before today
branches.cn: 落款为七天前的那封信

branches.en: a lake that filled this valley in a story's opening line
branches.cn: 故事开头那句里填满山谷的湖

branches.en: an old photograph with no date on the back
branches.cn: 背面没写日期的旧照片

branches.en: one backward glance, now counted and now only felt
branches.cn: 同一个回望，有时数得清，有时只凭感觉

intro.en: An Old English prefix of departure, a verb of going, and the worn remains of a participle ending.
intro.cn: 一个表示「离开」的古英语前缀、一个表示「走」的动词，以及被磨损的过去分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: This word is Germanic, not Latin, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语来源，并非拉丁语，因此拉丁词条列表为空。

items.meaning: to move from one place to another

definition_zh: 同意；答应；商定；相符；适合
definition_en: to share the same opinion, to say yes to a request, to reach a shared decision, or to be consistent with something
core_image: 两个人原本朝相反方向，最后转向同一个方向
scene: 两个人隔着桌子对视，其中一人先伸出手。After a long pause, he agreed to sign the contract.
sceneCN: 这里 agree 是「答应、应允」（第 2 个义项：对请求或建议表示同意并承诺去做）；句意为沉默良久之后，他答应签这份合同。图中可辨识物件：长桌、合同、伸出的手。

pos.zh: 动词：同意；答应；商定；相符；适合

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「协议；一致」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「令人愉快的；可接受的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「愉快地；欣然地」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不同意；有分歧」
由 disagree 加名词后缀构成，义为「分歧；争执」

senses.title: To share an opinion
senses.definition: to have the same opinion as another person
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人持相同的看法
senses.example: I agree with you about the schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 在日程安排上我同意你的看法。
senses.why: The oldest English sense is 'to be of one mind', which is why agree takes with when a person is the one being agreed with.
senses.whyCN: 英语里最古老的意思就是「同处一个心思」，所以与某人意见相同时，agree 后面用 with。

senses.title: To say yes to something
senses.definition: to say yes to a request, offer, or suggestion, committing yourself to it
senses.definitionCN: 对请求、提议或建议表示同意，并承诺照办
senses.example: After a long pause, he agreed to sign the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 沉默良久之后，他答应签这份合同。
senses.why: From sharing a view, the word moved to sharing a commitment: you agree to do what has been asked.
senses.whyCN: 从「看法相同」推进到「承担相同的事」：你答应去做别人请求你做的事。

senses.title: To settle something together
senses.definition: to reach a shared decision about a plan, price, or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 就计划、价格或安排共同作出决定
senses.example: The two sides agreed a price before lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在午饭前商定了价格。
senses.why: When two parties each give up part of their position, the result is an agreed thing, so the verb takes a direct object in business use.
senses.whyCN: 双方各让一步之后产生一个共同认可的结果，因此商业用法里这个动词可以直接带宾语。

senses.title: To be consistent with
senses.definition: of statements, figures, or accounts, to match or be consistent with one another
senses.definitionCN: 指陈述、数字或记述彼此吻合、不矛盾
senses.example: His account does not agree with the written record.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法与书面记录不符。
senses.why: Two accounts that match are like two minds that match, so the same verb describes facts falling into line.
senses.whyCN: 两份记述吻合，就像两个心思吻合，于是同一个动词也用来描述事实彼此对得上。

senses.title: To suit someone's body
senses.definition: of food, climate, or conditions, to suit a person's health or stomach
senses.definitionCN: 指食物、气候或环境适合某人的身体或肠胃
senses.example: Spicy food does not agree with me.
senses.exampleCN: 辣的食物不适合我的肠胃。
senses.why: This sense keeps the Latin root's original meaning 'to be pleasing': what agrees with you is literally what is pleasant to your body.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留了拉丁词根「令人愉快」的本义：agree with you 的东西，字面上就是让你的身体觉得舒服的东西。

intro.en: Agree comes from a Latin phrase meaning 'to be pleasing', and its road to 'share an opinion' passed through old French courtship and bargaining.
intro.cn: agree 来自一个意为「令人愉快」的拉丁说法，它走到「意见一致」这条路，经过了古法语的殷勤与讨价还价。

items.en: Gratus meant 'pleasing, welcome, acceptable', and it also gives gratitude and grateful.
items.cn: gratus 意为「令人愉快的、受欢迎的、可接受的」，gratitude 与 grateful 也出自它。

items.en: The phrase ad gratum, 'to what is pleasing', produced the verb agree in Vulgar Latin and Old French.
items.cn: 短语 ad gratum「合人心意」在通俗拉丁语与古法语中演化出动词。

items.en: Agreer meant 'to please, to be acceptable', and also 'to consent', since one consents to what pleases one.
items.cn: agreer 意为「使愉快、可接受」，也指「应允」，因为人总是应允令自己满意的事。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century, first in the sense 'to please' and soon 'to consent'.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个词，先有「使愉快」义，很快出现「应允」义。

items.en: The sense 'to hold the same opinion' became dominant, while 'food agrees with me' preserves the oldest meaning.
items.cn: 「持相同看法」成为主要义项，而「食物适合我」这一类说法保存了最古老的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on agree; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of consent, each with a different degree of commitment.
note.cn: 形近组收由 agree 构成的一族词；近义组收表示「同意」的动词，承诺程度各不相同。

entries.definition: A formal arrangement, or the state of sharing an opinion.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的约定，或意见一致的状态。

entries.definition: Pleasant, or willing to accept a suggestion.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的，或乐意接受建议的。

entries.definition: To hold a different opinion, or to fail to match.
entries.definitionCN: 持不同看法，或彼此不符。

entries.definition: To give permission for something, often formally.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事给予许可，通常较正式。

entries.definition: To agree with an opinion, used mainly in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 同意某种意见，主要用于正式书面语。

entries.definition: To consider something good or acceptable, often with authority.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事好或可接受，常含权威意味。

entries.definition: To express formal agreement, especially to a proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 正式表示同意，尤指对提议。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: the Latin preposition ad- and gratus, 'pleasing'.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：拉丁介词 ad- 与 gratus「令人愉快的」。

normal.en: Agree comes from 'to be pleasing', so what agrees with you was once simply what pleased you.
normal.cn: agree 来自「令人愉快」，所以 agree with you 的东西，最早就是让你舒服的东西。

normal.en: Agree with a person, agree to a plan, agree on a price: the preposition records what kind of agreement it is.
normal.cn: 对某人用 with，对计划用 to，对价格用 on：介词记录了这是哪一种同意。

normal.en: Agree has no -e before -ing: agreeing keeps the e to protect the long vowel.
normal.cn: agree 加 -ing 时保留 e：写作 agreeing，以保住长元音。

normal.en: The -d of agreed is pronounced like a t, a small trace of how English clips endings.
normal.cn: agreed 词尾的 d 读得像 t，这是英语压缩词尾留下的痕迹。

normal.en: Disagree is simply agree with a Latin 'apart' in front.
normal.cn: disagree 就是 agree 前面加了一个表示「分开」的拉丁前缀。

abstract.en: To agree is first to find something pleasant, then to find a shared position: pleasure comes before consensus.
abstract.cn: 同意先是觉得舒服，然后才找到共同立场：愉快感走在共识之前。

abstract.en: The five senses of agree map five kinds of fit: minds, commitments, deals, facts, and bodies.
abstract.cn: agree 的五个义项对应五种「合」：心思相合、承诺相合、交易相合、事实相合、身体相合。

abstract.en: A word that covers both opinions and digestion shows how far metaphor can stretch a single root.
abstract.cn: 一个词既管意见又管肠胃，说明比喻能把同一个词根拉多远。

examples.en: I agree with you about the schedule.
examples.cn: 在日程安排上我同意你的看法。

examples.en: They agreed to meet at the station at noon.
examples.cn: 他们约好中午在车站见面。

examples.en: The two accounts of the accident do not agree.
examples.cn: 关于这起事故的两份说法互相不符。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，格里」——额，格里也点头了，大家意见一致。

root: 源自拉丁语 gratus「令人愉快的」，短语 ad gratum「合人心意」经古法语 agreer 进入英语，由「使人满意」引申为「应允」与「意见一致」。

sensesIntro.en: One image of two parties turning the same way runs through all five senses: minds, promises, deals, records, and even stomachs can fall into line.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项贯穿着同一个「两方转向同一方向」的画面：心思、承诺、交易、记录，甚至肠胃，都可以对上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people facing opposite ways turn until they face the same direction.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个背向而立的人转过身，最后朝向同一个方向。

branches.en: two heads nodding at the same moment
branches.cn: 两个人同时点头

branches.en: a hand reaching out to take the pen
branches.cn: 伸出手去接那支笔

branches.en: a price written down and initialled by both sides
branches.cn: 被双方写下并签上首字母的价格

branches.en: two columns of figures that finally line up
branches.cn: 两列终于对齐的数字

branches.en: a meal that sits well in the stomach
branches.cn: 吃下去肠胃舒服的一顿饭

intro.en: A Latin adjective of pleasing, a preposition that points it, and the French verb endings English trimmed.
intro.cn: 一个表示「令人愉快」的拉丁形容词、一个给它定方向的介词，以及英语削短的法制动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: gratus and the phrase ad gratum are recorded Latin; the verb itself took shape in Vulgar Latin and Old French.
latinIntro.cn: gratus 与短语 ad gratum 都是有文献记录的拉丁语；动词本身在通俗拉丁语与古法语中成形。

definition_zh: 协议；协定；一致；同意；（语法）一致关系
definition_en: a formal arrangement between people or groups, the state of sharing the same opinion, or the matching of grammatical forms
core_image: 两份文件并排放着，落款处是两个不同的签名，内容却完全相同
scene: 会议室里两支笔几乎同时落在一份文件上。Both companies signed the agreement on Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 agreement 是「协议、协定」（第 1 个义项：双方正式达成的书面约定）；句意为两家公司在周五签署了这份协议。图中可辨识物件：文件、两支笔、会议桌。

pos.zh: 名词：协议；协定；一致；同意；（语法）一致关系

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词形式，义为「同意；商定」
由 agree 加形容词后缀构成，义为「令人愉快的；可接受的」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「分歧；争执」
由否定前缀加 agree 构成，义为「不同意」

senses.title: A formal arrangement
senses.definition: a formal arrangement or contract reached between two or more parties
senses.definitionCN: 两方或多方正式达成的安排或合同
senses.example: Both companies signed the agreement on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司在周五签署了这份协议。
senses.why: The -ment suffix turns the act of agreeing into its result, so the word names the settled thing that both sides can sign.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ment 把「同意」这个动作转成动作的结果，因此这个词指的就是双方可以签字的那份定下来的东西。

senses.title: The state of sharing a view
senses.definition: the state of having the same opinion, or the fact of people sharing a view
senses.definitionCN: 持有相同意见的状态，或人们看法相同这一事实
senses.example: There is broad agreement that the rule needs changing.
senses.exampleCN: 人们普遍认为这条规定需要修改。
senses.why: This is the abstract side of the same suffix: not the signed document but the shared mind behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这是同一词尾的抽象一面：不是签好的文件，而是文件背后那个相同的心思。

senses.title: Matching forms in grammar
senses.definition: in grammar, the matching of a verb with its subject, or of an adjective with its noun
senses.definitionCN: 语法上动词与主语、形容词与名词之间的形式对应
senses.example: Subject-verb agreement is tested in the first section.
senses.exampleCN: 主谓一致在第一部分考查。
senses.why: Grammarians borrowed the everyday sense of 'falling into line' to describe forms that must match each other.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家借用了日常义里「对齐」的意思，用来描述必须彼此对应的形式。

intro.en: Agreement is agree plus the French noun ending -ment, so it names both the act of agreeing and the thing agreed.
intro.cn: agreement 是 agree 加上法语名词词尾 -ment，既指「同意」这个动作，也指同意之后定下来的东西。

items.en: The root gratus meant 'pleasing, welcome', the source of agree and of gratitude.
items.cn: 词根 gratus 意为「令人愉快的、受欢迎的」，是 agree 与 gratitude 的来源。

items.en: Agreer meant 'to please' and 'to consent'; its noun agrement named the consent itself.
items.cn: agreer 意为「使愉快」与「应允」；其名词 agrement 指应允这件事。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the fifteenth century, and the spelling settled as agreement later.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个名词，拼写后来才固定为 agreement。

items.en: The legal sense 'a binding arrangement' develops first, with the abstract sense 'shared opinion' alongside it.
items.cn: 「有约束力的约定」这一法律义先发展出来，「共同看法」这一抽象义同时存在。

items.en: The grammatical sense is added in the nineteenth century, when English grammar writing turned to Latin models.
items.cn: 语法义在十九世纪加入，当时英语语法写作正大量借用拉丁语法模型。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the agree family; the near-meaning group gathers documents and states of accord that differ in formality.
note.cn: 形近组收 agree 词族；近义组收表示「约定」的文件与「一致」状态，正式程度各不相同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to share an opinion or consent.
entries.definitionCN: 表示意见相同或应允的动词。

entries.definition: Pleasant, or willing to go along with something.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的，或乐意配合的。

entries.definition: A failure to agree, or a quarrel about it.
entries.definitionCN: 未能达成一致，或由此产生的争执。

entries.definition: A legally binding written arrangement between parties.
entries.definitionCN: 各方之间具有法律约束力的书面约定。

entries.definition: A formal agreement between states, usually signed and ratified.
entries.definitionCN: 国家之间的正式协议，通常需签署并批准。

entries.definition: A general agreement reached by a group as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 一个群体整体达成的普遍共识。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: the verb agree and the French noun ending -ment.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：动词 agree 与法语名词词尾 -ment。

normal.en: Agreement is agree plus -ment: the suffix turns the act into the thing.
normal.cn: agreement 是 agree 加 -ment：词尾把动作变成那个东西。

normal.en: You sign an agreement but you are in agreement; one is a document, the other a state.
normal.cn: 你签署一份协议，但你是「处于一致之中」；一个是文件，一个是状态。

normal.en: Spell it with -ment, not -mant: the vowel before the ending is e, as in agree.
normal.cn: 词尾是 -ment 不是 -mant：结尾前的元音是 e，跟 agree 一致。

normal.en: Subject-verb agreement is just two forms falling into line, the same image as two parties.
normal.cn: 主谓一致不过是两个形式对齐，和双方达成一致是同一幅画面。

normal.en: A verbal agreement is still an agreement, though nothing is written down.
normal.cn: 口头协议仍是协议，只是没有写在纸上。

abstract.en: An agreement is a promise made durable: the shared mind is fixed in a form that outlasts the conversation.
abstract.cn: 协议是让承诺变得耐久：共同的心思被固定成一种比谈话活得更久的形式。

abstract.en: The same word covers a contract and a mood, because both are ways of things lining up.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指合同又指气氛，因为两者都是事物对齐的方式。

abstract.en: Grammar's use of agreement shows how deeply the idea of matching runs in language about language.
abstract.cn: 语法里也用 agreement，说明「彼此对应」这个观念在谈论语言时扎得多深。

examples.en: Both companies signed the agreement on Friday.
examples.cn: 两家公司在周五签署了这份协议。

examples.en: There is broad agreement that the rule needs changing.
examples.cn: 人们普遍认为这条规定需要修改。

examples.en: The teacher marked every agreement error in the essay.
examples.cn: 老师标出了文章中每一处一致关系错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，格里门特」——额，格里门特先生在两份文件上都签了字。

root: 由 agree 加名词词尾 -ment 构成；agree 源自拉丁语 gratus「令人愉快的」，经古法语 agreer「应允」进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses come from one act of lining up: a signed result, a shared mind, and grammatical forms that must match.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都来自同一个「对齐」的动作：签下来的结果、共同的心思，以及必须彼此对应的语法形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two documents side by side, each with a different signature, but with identical wording.
core.cn: 核心意象：两份文件并排放着，签名不同，文字却一模一样。

branches.en: a contract initialled on the last page
branches.cn: 在末页签上首字母的合同

branches.en: a room of heads nodding together
branches.cn: 一屋子人一起点头

branches.en: a verb that changes to match its subject
branches.cn: 随主语变化形式的动词

branches.en: a committee report that says the members concur
branches.cn: 写着成员意见一致的委员会报告

branches.en: one matching idea, from signatures to syntax
branches.cn: 同一个「对应」观念，从签名一路走到句法

intro.en: The verb agree, the French noun ending -ment, and the negative prefix that reverses it.
intro.cn: 动词 agree、法语名词词尾 -ment，以及把意思反转的否定前缀。

latinIntro.en: Only the root gratus is Latin; the noun itself was formed in French.
latinIntro.cn: 只有词根 gratus 属拉丁语，名词本身是在法语中构成的。

definition_zh: 农业；农耕；农学
definition_en: the practice of farming, including growing crops and raising animals, or the science that studies it
core_image: 一块被犁开的田，垄沟笔直，尽头是尚未收割的麦子
scene: 清晨的田里，拖拉机刚翻过一道土埂，泥土还冒着湿气。Agriculture still employs most of the people in this valley.
sceneCN: 这里 agriculture 是「农业、农耕」（第 1 个义项：种植作物与饲养牲畜的生产活动）；句意为这个山谷里大多数人仍以农业为生。图中可辨识物件：拖拉机、犁沟、麦田。

pos.zh: 名词：农业；农耕；农学

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「农业的；农艺的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「在农业上」
由本词加表人后缀构成，义为「农学家；农业经营者」
由 agri- 与 business 合成，义为「农业综合企业」

senses.title: The practice of farming
senses.definition: the work and practice of growing crops and raising animals for food, fibre, or fuel
senses.definitionCN: 种植作物、饲养牲畜以获取食物、纤维或燃料的生产活动
senses.example: Agriculture still employs most of the people in this valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷里大多数人仍以农业为生。
senses.why: The Latin parts mean 'field' and 'cultivation', so the word names the whole working relationship between people and soil.
senses.whyCN: 两个拉丁部件分别意为「田地」与「耕作」，所以这个词命名的是人与土地之间整套劳作关系。

senses.title: The academic study of farming
senses.definition: the science or university subject that studies farming methods, soils, and crop production
senses.definitionCN: 研究耕作方法、土壤与作物生产的科学或大学学科
senses.example: She studied agriculture before joining the seed company.
senses.exampleCN: 她进种子公司之前学的是农学。
senses.why: When the word entered university titles, the practice became a discipline, so the same noun can name a degree subject.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词进入大学系科名称，耕作实践就成了一门学科，于是同一个名词也能指一个学位专业。

intro.en: Agriculture is a transparent Latin compound: a field plus its cultivation, put together by Roman writers on farming.
intro.cn: agriculture 是一个透明的拉丁复合词：田地加上耕作，由罗马的农书作者拼合而成。

items.en: Ager meant 'field, farmland', and it survives in acre and in the agri- of many English words.
items.cn: ager 意为「田地、耕地」，在 acre 以及英语许多词的 agri- 中留存下来。

items.en: Cultura meant 'tending, cultivation', from colere 'to till, worship', and it also gives culture.
items.cn: cultura 意为「照料、耕作」，出自 colere「耕种、敬奉」，culture 也源自它。

items.en: The compound agricultura is recorded in Roman agricultural writing such as Columella and Pliny.
items.cn: 复合词 agricultura 见于科卢梅拉、普林尼等罗马农书。

items.en: French formed agriculture from the Latin elements, and English took it from French in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语用这些拉丁成分构成 agriculture，英语在十六世纪从法语借入。

items.en: The word widened from the work itself to the industry and the academic subject, giving agricultural and agriculturist.
items.cn: 这个词从劳作本身扩展到产业与学科，并派生出 agricultural 与 agriculturist。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin field-and-tilling family; the near-meaning group gathers kinds of farming, each with a different scope.
note.cn: 形近组收「田地与耕作」这一拉丁词族；近义组收各种农业说法，范围各不相同。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning relating to farming.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为与农业有关的。

entries.definition: A person who practises or studies farming.
entries.definitionCN: 从事农业或研究农学的人。

entries.definition: The shared way of life of a people, originally 'cultivation' of the mind or soil.
entries.definitionCN: 一个民族共同的生活方式，本义是对心灵或土地的耕作。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the activity of growing crops and keeping animals.
entries.definitionCN: 指种庄稼、养牲畜这一活动的日常说法。

entries.definition: The careful management of soil, crops, or animals.
entries.definitionCN: 对土壤、作物或牲畜的精心管理。

entries.definition: The science of crop production and soil management.
entries.definitionCN: 研究作物生产与土壤管理的科学。

normalIntro.en: Two real Latin parts carry the word: ager, 'field', and cultura, 'tending'.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实的拉丁部件承载这个词：ager「田地」与 cultura「耕作」。

normal.en: Agri- is field, as in acre; culture is tending, as in cultivate: agriculture is field-tending.
normal.cn: agri- 是田地，见 acre；culture 是照料，见 cultivate：agriculture 就是照料田地。

normal.en: Culture grew out of the same farming word, because growing a mind was imagined like growing a crop.
normal.cn: culture 也出自同一个耕作词，因为「培养心智」被想象成「种庄稼」。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable: AG-ri-cul-ture.
normal.cn: 重音落在第一个音节：AG-ri-cul-ture。

normal.en: Add -al and you get agricultural, the adjective used for policy and land.
normal.cn: 加 -al 得到 agricultural，是用于政策与土地上的形容词。

normal.en: Keep the middle syllable clear: cul, not cle, before -ture.
normal.cn: 注意中间的音节是 cul 而不是 cle，后面才是 -ture。

abstract.en: Agriculture is the oldest technology: it turns soil, water and sunlight into a predictable food supply.
abstract.cn: 农业是最古老的技术：它把土壤、水和阳光变成可预期的食物供应。

abstract.en: That the same word produced culture suggests that civilisations saw themselves as something to be cultivated.
abstract.cn: 同一个词还生出 culture，说明文明把自己看作需要耕作的东西。

abstract.en: Naming farming as a science changes who holds the knowledge: the field becomes a laboratory.
abstract.cn: 把农耕称作一门科学，就改变了知识掌握在谁手里：田变成了实验室。

examples.en: Agriculture still employs most of the people in this valley.
examples.cn: 这个山谷里大多数人仍以农业为生。

examples.en: The country's economy depends heavily on agriculture.
examples.cn: 这个国家的经济严重依赖农业。

examples.en: She studied agriculture before joining the seed company.
examples.cn: 她进种子公司之前学的是农学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱割麦，靠它扯」——爱割麦子，日子就靠它撑着，这就是农业。

root: 源自拉丁语 agricultura，由 ager「田地」与 cultura「耕作」复合而成，本义即「耕种田地」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses name the same relation between people and soil: one as daily work, the other as a subject studied in a lecture hall.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项命名的是人与土地之间同一种关系：一个是日常劳作，一个是在讲堂里被研究的学问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ploughed field with straight furrows, ending in grain that has not yet been cut.
core.cn: 核心意象：犁过的田，垄沟笔直，尽头是尚未收割的麦子。

branches.en: a tractor turning the earth at dawn
branches.cn: 天亮时翻地的拖拉机

branches.en: cattle led back to the shed at dusk
branches.cn: 黄昏时被赶回棚里的牛

branches.en: a lecture on soil acidity
branches.cn: 一堂讲土壤酸度的课

branches.en: a field trial written up in a journal
branches.cn: 写成论文发表的田间试验

branches.en: one field, worked by hand and studied by book
branches.cn: 同一块田，既用手耕作，也用书研究

intro.en: A Latin noun for field, a Latin noun for tending, and the English endings built on them.
intro.cn: 一个意为「田地」的拉丁名词、一个意为「耕作」的拉丁名词，以及建在其上的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: ager and cultura are recorded Latin; the compound agricultura is attested in Roman farming writers.
latinIntro.cn: ager 与 cultura 都是有文献记录的拉丁词，复合词 agricultura 见于罗马农书。

items.meaning: one who farms or studies farming

definition_zh: 在前面；向前；提前；领先；（时间上）今后
definition_en: in front, further forward, earlier than expected, or in a better position than others
core_image: 一个人走在队伍最前面，身后的人还在追赶
scene: 雪后的山路只剩一条窄窄的车辙，司机握紧方向盘。The road ahead was blocked by snow.
sceneCN: 这里 ahead 是「在前面」（第 1 个义项：在空间上位于前方）；句意为前面的路被雪堵住了。图中可辨识物件：车辙、雪堆、方向盘。

pos.zh: 副词：在前面；向前；提前；领先

derivatives.zh: 由 go 与 ahead 合成的名词，义为「许可；放行」
由 straight 与 ahead 合成的形容词，义为「一直向前的；直截了当的」

senses.title: In front, further forward
senses.definition: in a position in front of someone or something, or further forward along a route
senses.definitionCN: 位于某人或某物之前，或沿路更靠前的位置
senses.example: The road ahead was blocked by snow.
senses.exampleCN: 前面的路被雪堵住了。
senses.why: Ahead was formed from a- 'on' and head, so it originally meant 'at the head', the position at the front of a line.
senses.whyCN: ahead 由 a-「在」与 head「头」构成，本义是「在头部的位置」，也就是队伍最前方。

senses.title: Earlier than planned
senses.definition: before the expected or planned time
senses.definitionCN: 在预期或计划的时间之前
senses.example: We finished the survey two days ahead of schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 我们比计划提前两天完成了调查。
senses.why: If you are ahead on a road, you arrive before others; time borrowed the same image, so being ahead of schedule means arriving early.
senses.whyCN: 在路上走在前面的人会先到；时间借用了同一个画面，所以 ahead of schedule 就是比预定时间先到。

senses.title: In a leading position
senses.definition: in a better position than others, especially in a competition or ranking
senses.definitionCN: 在竞争或排名中处于比别人更有利的位置
senses.example: Our team is ahead by two goals.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队领先两个球。
senses.why: The front of the line became the front of the scoreboard: whoever is further forward is winning.
senses.whyCN: 队伍的最前端变成了记分牌的最前端：位置更靠前的人就是赢的那一方。

senses.title: In the future
senses.definition: of time, in the future, especially when referring to what is still to come
senses.definitionCN: 指时间上尚未到来的部分，尤指将要面对的事
senses.example: There are hard decisions ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 前面还有艰难的决定要做。
senses.why: Since we imagine the future as a road in front of us, what lies ahead is simply what has not been reached yet.
senses.whyCN: 因为人把未来想象成眼前的一条路，所以 lies ahead 的东西就是尚未走到的东西。

intro.en: Ahead is a simple English compound of a preposition and a body part, and it has been pointing forwards since the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: ahead 是介词加身体部位的简单英语复合词，从十七世纪起就一直指向前方。

items.en: Heafod meant 'head', the front and top of the body, and it also named the leader of a group.
items.cn: hēafod 意为「头」，是身体最前最高的部分，也用来指一群人的首领。

items.en: The prefix a- came from Old English an, 'on', and it formed phrases such as on head and a head.
items.cn: 前缀 a- 出自古英语 an「在……上」，构成 on head、a head 这类说法。

items.en: The two elements fused into ahead, first in nautical use for the front of a ship.
items.cn: 两个成分融合成 ahead，最初用于航海，指船的前方。

items.en: The word spread from ships to roads, races and schedules, gaining the senses 'leading' and 'earlier'.
items.cn: 这个词从船上扩展到道路、比赛与日程，获得「领先」与「提前」两个义项。

items.en: The time sense, as in 'the years ahead', is now as common as the physical one.
items.cn: 表示时间的用法，如 the years ahead，如今与表示空间的用法一样常见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that resemble ahead in form; the near-meaning group gathers ways of saying 'in front' or 'earlier'.
note.cn: 形近组收外形与 ahead 相近的词；近义组收表示「在前」或「更早」的各种说法。

entries.definition: The body part, or the front or leader of something.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的头部，或某物的前端、领导者。

entries.definition: A written form of a cough used to attract attention.
entries.definitionCN: 用来引起注意的咳嗽声的书面写法。

entries.definition: In preparation or happening, as in 'something is afoot'.
entries.definitionCN: 在准备中或正在发生，如 something is afoot。

entries.definition: Towards the front, or towards a point in the future.
entries.definitionCN: 朝前方，或朝未来的某一点。

entries.definition: At the front of something, often in a literal physical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 在某物的前面，多指具体空间位置。

entries.definition: Earlier than a particular event, usually by preparation.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一事件之前，通常指事先准备。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: the prefix a-, 'on', and head.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：前缀 a-「在」与 head。

normal.en: Ahead is 'on head', and the head of a line is its front.
normal.cn: ahead 就是「在头上」，而队伍的头就是最前面。

normal.en: All four senses follow the same line: in front in space, in time, and on the scoreboard.
normal.cn: 四个义项都沿着同一条线：空间在前、时间在前、记分牌在前。

normal.en: Go ahead is literally 'go to the front', which is why it means 'please continue'.
normal.cn: go ahead 字面上是「走到前面去」，所以它等于「请继续」。

normal.en: Keep the two parts visible in spelling: a-head, one h.
normal.cn: 拼写时让两个部件都看得见：a-head，只有一个 h。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable: a-HEAD.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-HEAD。

abstract.en: We speak of time as a road, which is why a word for the front of a line also means the future.
abstract.cn: 人把时间说成一条路，所以一个表示队伍最前端的词，也用来表示未来。

abstract.en: Being ahead is always relative: the word quietly assumes someone else is behind.
abstract.cn: 「在前面」永远是相对的：这个词悄悄预设了有人落在后面。

abstract.en: Ahead turns a body part into a direction, a reminder that abstract space words often begin with the body.
abstract.cn: ahead 把身体部位变成一个方向词，提醒我们抽象的空间词常常从身体开始。

examples.en: The road ahead was blocked by snow.
examples.cn: 前面的路被雪堵住了。

examples.en: We finished the survey two days ahead of schedule.
examples.cn: 我们比计划提前两天完成了调查。

examples.en: There are hard decisions ahead.
examples.cn: 前面还有艰难的决定要做。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，黑的」——额，黑的前面那段路，什么也看不清。

root: 由古英语介词 an「在……上」弱化成的 a- 与 head「头」复合而成，本义「在头部、在最前方」。

sensesIntro.en: One image of standing at the front of a line serves all four senses: in space, in time, in rank, and in the future.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项共用同一个「站在队伍最前面」的画面：空间上在前、时间上在前、名次上在前，以及尚未到来的将来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one walker at the front of a column, the rest still catching up behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人走在队伍最前面，其余的人还在后面追赶。

branches.en: a snow-covered road that disappears round a bend
branches.cn: 在转弯处消失的雪路

branches.en: a report handed in before the deadline
branches.cn: 截止日期前交上去的报告

branches.en: a scoreboard with one side two goals clear
branches.cn: 一方领先两球的记分牌

branches.en: a row of unopened letters on the desk
branches.cn: 桌上那一排还没拆的信

branches.en: one front position, read as space and as time
branches.cn: 同一个「在前」的位置，既读作空间也读作时间

intro.en: An Old English preposition worn down to a prefix, joined to a noun for the head.
intro.cn: 一个磨损成前缀的古英语介词，加上一个表示「头」的名词。

latinIntro.en: This word is Germanic, not Latin, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语来源，并非拉丁语，因此拉丁词条列表为空。

items.meaningCN: 一直向前的；直截了当的

definition_zh: 帮助；援助；辅助器具；有助于
definition_en: help or support given to someone, a thing that helps, or to help something happen
core_image: 一只伸过来的手，托住快要倒下的那一侧
scene: 洪水退去后，村口停着几辆送物资的卡车。The village received aid after the flood.
sceneCN: 这里 aid 是「援助、救济」（第 1 个义项：给予他人的帮助或物资支持）；句意为洪水过后这个村子收到了援助。图中可辨识物件：卡车、纸箱、泥泞的村口。

pos.zh: 名词：帮助；援助；辅助器具
动词：帮助；有助于；促进

derivatives.zh: 同源异体词，义为「助手；（要人的）助理」
由否定前缀加过去分词构成，义为「无援助的；独自的」
由动词加 -ing 构成的动名词，义为「帮助的行为」

senses.title: Help given to someone
senses.definition: help or support, especially in the form of money, food, or services given to people in need
senses.definitionCN: 给予需要者的帮助或支持，尤指钱款、食物或服务
senses.example: The village received aid after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后这个村子收到了援助。
senses.why: Aid is an uncountable noun because it names help as a mass, not one countable act, which is why we say some aid rather than an aid in this sense.
senses.whyCN: aid 作这个义项时不可数，因为它把帮助看成一团总量，而不是一次可数的行为，所以说 some aid 而不是 an aid。

senses.title: A device that helps
senses.definition: a physical object or tool that helps a person do something
senses.definitionCN: 帮助人完成某事的实物或工具
senses.example: A walking aid helped him cross the room.
senses.exampleCN: 一件助行器具帮他走过了房间。
senses.why: Here the help is concentrated into a countable object, so the same word shifts from mass help to a single thing you can hold.
senses.whyCN: 这里的帮助被凝聚成一件可数的实物，于是同一个词从「一团帮助」变成「一件能拿在手里的东西」。

senses.title: To help something happen
senses.definition: to help or make it easier for something to happen or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 帮助或使某事更容易发生、更容易成功
senses.example: The map aided us in finding the path.
senses.exampleCN: 那张地图帮我们找到了小路。
senses.why: The verb keeps the noun's meaning but adds direction: the help is now an action that pushes a result forward.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了名词的意思，却加上了方向：帮助变成了推动某个结果向前的一个动作。

intro.en: Aid came from French, and behind the French word stands a Latin verb of helping built on a root meaning 'help'.
intro.cn: aid 来自法语，而法语背后是一个拉丁语「帮助」动词，其词根意为「援助」。

items.en: Adiuvare meant 'to help, assist', formed from ad- 'to' and a verb of giving help.
items.cn: adiuvare 意为「帮助、支援」，由 ad-「向」与一个表示给予帮助的动词构成。

items.en: The frequentative adiutare, 'to keep helping', became the everyday form in later Latin.
items.cn: 表反复的 adiutare「不断帮助」在晚期拉丁语中成为日常形式。

items.en: Old French aide meant both 'help' and 'a helper', and English borrowed both meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 aide 既指「帮助」，也指「帮手」，英语把两个意思都借了进来。

items.en: English records aid in the fourteenth century as a noun and soon after as a verb.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪记录到名词 aid，不久后出现动词用法。

items.en: The spelling aide was revived later for a personal assistant, leaving aid for help in general.
items.cn: 拼写 aide 后来被重新启用，专门指人的助理，aid 则留给一般意义上的帮助。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that look like aid but are not synonyms; the near-meaning group gathers help and relief with different force.
note.cn: 形近组收外形像 aid 却并非同义的词；近义组收帮助与救济，力度各不相同。

entries.definition: A personal assistant, especially to a senior political figure.
entries.definitionCN: 私人助理，尤指高级政要的助手。

entries.definition: A sudden attack or an unexpected police search.
entries.definitionCN: 突然袭击，或警方的突击搜查。

entries.definition: A female servant, or a young unmarried woman in older use.
entries.definitionCN: 女仆，旧时也指未婚年轻女子。

entries.definition: The broad everyday word for making things easier for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 日常最宽泛的「帮助」说法。

entries.definition: To help someone do something, often in a supporting role.
entries.definitionCN: 协助某人做某事，常指辅助角色。

entries.definition: Money, food, or help given to people in a disaster or crisis.
entries.definitionCN: 在灾难或危机中给予的钱款、食物或救助。

normalIntro.en: Two real layers carry the word: the Latin verb adiutare and its French descendant aide.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实层次承载这个词：拉丁动词 adiutare 及其法语后裔 aide。

normal.en: Aid and aide sound the same; the e marks the person, the bare word marks the help.
normal.cn: aid 与 aide 同音；带 e 的指人，不带 e 的指帮助。

normal.en: First aid is the help given first, before doctors arrive.
normal.cn: first aid 就是医生到来之前最先给出的那份帮助。

normal.en: The verb aid is short and stays short: aided, aiding, no doubling.
normal.cn: 动词 aid 很短，变形也保持简短：aided、aiding，不加倍写辅音。

normal.en: A hearing aid is help shrunk into a small device.
normal.cn: 助听器就是把「帮助」缩进一个小装置里。

normal.en: In aid of means 'in order to help', the oldest sense still visible.
normal.cn: in aid of 意为「为了帮助」，最古老的意思还看得见。

abstract.en: Aid makes dependence visible: the hand that helps also records who is in need.
abstract.cn: 援助让依赖关系变得可见：伸出的那只手同时也记录了谁需要帮助。

abstract.en: The same word covers money, a walking stick and a small act of assistance, because all three remove an obstacle.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指钱款、又指拐杖和一次小小的帮忙，因为三者都在移除某个障碍。

abstract.en: Foreign aid shows how a word of kindness can become an instrument of policy.
abstract.cn: 对外援助显示了善意的词如何变成政策的工具。

examples.en: The village received aid after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后这个村子收到了援助。

examples.en: A walking aid helped him cross the room.
examples.cn: 一件助行器具帮他走过了房间。

examples.en: The map aided us in finding the path.
examples.cn: 那张地图帮我们找到了小路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶的」——诶，得有人递把手，这就是帮助。

root: 源自古法语 aide「帮助、帮手」，其前身为拉丁语 adiutare「不断帮助」，出自 adiuvare「帮助」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses remove an obstacle: help as a mass, help as an object, and help as an action.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都在移除障碍：作为总量的帮助、作为器物的帮助，以及作为动作的帮助。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches across and holds up the side that is about to fall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸过来，托住快要倒下的那一侧。

branches.en: boxes unloaded at a flooded village gate
branches.cn: 在受灾村口卸下的纸箱

branches.en: a bandage applied before the ambulance comes
branches.cn: 救护车到来前缠上的绷带

branches.en: a stick that takes the weight off one leg
branches.cn: 替一条腿分担重量的拐杖

branches.en: a map that shortens a search
branches.cn: 缩短了寻找时间的那张地图

branches.en: one helping hand, now a gift and now an action
branches.cn: 同一只援助之手，有时是馈赠，有时是动作

intro.en: A Latin verb of helping, its French descendant, and the English endings that build the family.
intro.cn: 一个表示「帮助」的拉丁动词、它的法语后裔，以及构成词族的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: adiuvare and adiutare are recorded Latin; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: adiuvare 与 adiutare 都是有文献记录的拉丁词，更早的印欧词根属重构。

definition_zh: （要人的）助手；助理；副官
definition_en: an assistant to a senior person, especially a political leader or military officer
core_image: 走在要人半步之后、随时递上文件的那个人
scene: 走廊尽头，一位年轻人快步跟上部长，把一张纸条递过去。A senior aide handed the minister a note.
sceneCN: 这里 aide 是「（要人的）助手」（第 1 个义项：为高级人物处理事务的助理）；句意为一名高级助理把一张便条递给部长。图中可辨识物件：走廊、纸条、公文包。

pos.zh: 名词：（要人的）助手；助理；副官

derivatives.zh: 由法语借入的军事用语，义为「副官；侍从武官」
由法语借入的外交用语，义为「备忘录；备忘便览」

senses.title: An assistant to a senior figure
senses.definition: a person employed to assist a senior political figure or official, often handling information and arrangements
senses.definitionCN: 受雇协助高级政治人物或官员的人，常负责信息与事务安排
senses.example: A senior aide handed the minister a note.
senses.exampleCN: 一名高级助理把一张便条递给部长。
senses.why: The e was added in the nineteenth century to separate the person from aid 'help', so the spelling itself marks the human role.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪加上 e，是为了把「人」与表示「帮助」的 aid 区分开，所以拼写本身就标出了这个人的身份。

senses.title: A military officer attending a superior
senses.definition: an officer whose duty is to attend a senior officer and carry orders, in the phrase aide-de-camp
senses.definitionCN: 负责随侍上级军官并传达命令的军官，用于 aide-de-camp 一词
senses.example: The general's aide-de-camp rode ahead to warn the camp.
senses.exampleCN: 将军的副官骑马先行，去给营地报信。
senses.why: This is the older military sense, borrowed whole from French, and it keeps the full French phrase rather than the short English form.
senses.whyCN: 这是更早的军事义，整组从法语借来，因此保留完整法语短语，而不是缩成英语的短形式。

intro.en: Aide and aid are the same French word twice borrowed: once for help, once for the person who gives it.
intro.cn: aide 与 aid 是同一个法语词被借了两次：一次指帮助，一次指提供帮助的人。

items.en: Adiutare, 'to keep helping', is the Latin verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: adiutare「不断帮助」是这整个词族背后的拉丁动词。

items.en: Old French aide could mean 'help' or 'a helper', so one form served both ideas.
items.cn: 古法语 aide 既可指「帮助」，也可指「帮手」，一个形式承担两个意思。

items.en: English took the word as aid in the fourteenth century, using it for both the help and the helper.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪以 aid 的形式借入，既指帮助也指帮手。

items.en: The spelling aide was revived for the personal assistant, following the French spelling, to keep the two roles apart.
items.cn: 十九世纪依照法语拼写重新启用 aide 专指私人助理，以便把两种角色分开。

items.en: Aide now covers political staff and, in the full French phrase, military officers, while aid stays with help in general.
items.cn: 如今 aide 指政治幕僚，在完整法语短语中亦指军官，而 aid 仍指一般意义上的帮助。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words confused with aide in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers people who assist, with different ranks.
note.cn: 形近组收易与 aide 拼写混淆的词；近义组收提供协助的人，身份层级各不相同。

entries.definition: Help itself, or the act of helping.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助本身，或提供帮助的行为。

entries.definition: A military officer who attends a senior officer.
entries.definitionCN: 随侍高级军官的军官。

entries.definition: A memorandum, or a document used to help the memory.
entries.definitionCN: 备忘录，或帮助记忆的文件。

entries.definition: A person who helps someone in their work, at any level.
entries.definitionCN: 在工作中帮助他人的人，层级不限。

entries.definition: A person whose role is to give expert advice.
entries.definitionCN: 专门提供专业建议的人。

entries.definition: A person who acts for a superior when needed.
entries.definitionCN: 在需要时代理上级职务的人。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: the French noun aide and the added e that marks a person.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：法语名词 aide，以及用来标记「人」的那个 e。

normal.en: The e is the person: aide has someone in it, aid is just help.
normal.cn: 那个 e 就是人：aide 里装着一个人，aid 只是帮助。

normal.en: An aide walks half a step behind and carries the papers.
normal.cn: 助手总是落后半步，手里抱着文件。

normal.en: Aide-de-camp keeps the whole French phrase, so it looks long even though the short form is tiny.
normal.cn: aide-de-camp 保留整个法语短语，所以短形式虽短，它却很长。

normal.en: Say it exactly like aid: the e is silent.
normal.cn: 发音与 aid 完全相同：结尾的 e 不发音。

normal.en: Presidential aide, senior aide, close aide: the adjective tells you how near the power the person stands.
normal.cn: 总统助手、高级助理、亲信助手：前面的形容词说明这个人离权力有多近。

abstract.en: An aide turns help into a job: the same old idea of assistance, now with hours and duties.
abstract.cn: 助手把帮助变成了一份职业：同样是「协助」这个古老观念，现在有了工时和职责。

abstract.en: That the helper needed a separate spelling shows how much a society cares about distinguishing a person from an act.
abstract.cn: 连「帮手」都需要单独的拼写，说明社会有多在意把一个人与一个动作区分开。

abstract.en: Proximity is the aide's real power: standing close to the decision is often more useful than making it.
abstract.cn: 接近性正是助手的真正权力：站在决定旁边，往往比做决定更有用。

examples.en: A senior aide handed the minister a note.
examples.cn: 一名高级助理把一张便条递给部长。

examples.en: She worked as an aide to the mayor for three years.
examples.cn: 她给市长当了三年助手。

examples.en: The general's aide-de-camp rode ahead to warn the camp.
examples.cn: 将军的副官骑马先行，去给营地报信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶的」——诶，得有个助理在旁边递文件。

root: 源自古法语 aide「帮助、帮手」，与 aid 同源；十九世纪依法语拼写重新启用 aide，专指要人的助理。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses name a person whose job is help: one in a political office, one on a general's staff.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都指以「帮助」为职责的人：一个在政治办公室里，一个在将军的幕僚中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young assistant half a step behind the senior figure, papers already in hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：年轻助手落后要人半步，文件已经拿在手里。

branches.en: a note passed in a corridor
branches.cn: 在走廊里递过去的一张便条

branches.en: a campaign worker keeping a candidate on time
branches.cn: 让候选人准时的竞选工作人员

branches.en: an officer riding ahead with orders
branches.cn: 带着命令先行出发的军官

branches.en: a uniform waiting at the door of a staff car
branches.cn: 在指挥车门口等候的军装

branches.en: one attending role, in civil and in military dress
branches.cn: 同一个随侍角色，一身文职、一身军装

intro.en: The French noun aide, its Latin verb, and the compound phrases French handed to English whole.
intro.cn: 法语名词 aide、其拉丁动词，以及法语整组交给英语的复合短语。

latinIntro.en: adiutare is recorded Latin; the French forms are medieval, and the military phrase is later still.
latinIntro.cn: adiutare 是有文献记录的拉丁词；法语形式属中世纪，军事短语出现更晚。

items.meaning: marks the person, not the help

definition_zh: 瞄准；旨在；目标；针对
definition_en: to point something at a target, to intend to achieve something, or the purpose one intends to reach
core_image: 弓弦拉开，箭尖对准远处那一点
scene: 院子里光线正好，她蹲下来，把镜头对准枝头那只鸟。She aimed the camera at the bird.
sceneCN: 这里 aim 是「把……对准」（第 1 个义项：让武器或器具指向目标）；句意为她把相机对准了那只鸟。图中可辨识物件：相机、树枝、鸟。

pos.zh: 动词：瞄准；对准；旨在；针对
名词：目标；目的；瞄准

derivatives.zh: 由本词加否定后缀构成，义为「无目标的；漫无目的的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「漫无目的地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「无目标的状态」

senses.title: To point at a target
senses.definition: to point a weapon, tool, or device towards a target
senses.definitionCN: 把武器、工具或器具指向某个目标
senses.example: She aimed the camera at the bird.
senses.exampleCN: 她把相机对准了那只鸟。
senses.why: The word came from French aesmer, 'to estimate', because aiming is judging distance and direction before you let go.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自法语 aesmer「估量」，因为瞄准就是出手之前先判断距离与方向。

senses.title: To intend to achieve
senses.definition: to plan or intend to achieve a particular result
senses.definitionCN: 计划或意图达成某个结果
senses.example: The campaign aims to cut waste by half.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动旨在把浪费减少一半。
senses.why: Once the arrow is pointed, the intention is fixed; the word moved from physical pointing to pointing a plan at an outcome.
senses.whyCN: 箭一指向，意图就定了；这个词于是从物理上的对准，转成把计划对准某个结果。

senses.title: A purpose or goal
senses.definition: the purpose or result that someone intends to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 某人想要达到的目的或结果
senses.example: Our aim is to finish the report by June.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的目标是在六月前完成这份报告。
senses.why: The noun keeps the picture of a mark to be hit, so an aim is simply the point at which the effort is directed.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了「待命中的靶点」这个画面，所以 aim 就是努力所指向的那一点。

senses.title: To direct something at a person
senses.definition: to direct a remark, product, or action at a particular person or group
senses.definitionCN: 把言论、产品或行动指向特定的人或群体
senses.example: The joke was aimed at the new intern.
senses.exampleCN: 那个玩笑是针对新来的实习生的。
senses.why: A person can be a target as easily as a mark, so aiming expands from arrows to words and products.
senses.whyCN: 人可以像靶子一样成为目标，于是 aim 从箭矢扩展到言语与商品。

intro.en: Aim came into English from French, and behind the French verb lies a Latin verb of estimating.
intro.cn: aim 从法语进入英语，而法语动词背后是一个表示「估量」的拉丁动词。

items.en: Aestimare meant 'to value, estimate, judge', the source of estimate and esteem.
items.cn: aestimare 意为「估价、估量、判断」，estimate 与 esteem 也出自它。

items.en: Aesmer meant 'to estimate, reckon', and in hunting and archery 'to aim'.
items.cn: aesmer 意为「估量、推算」，在狩猎与射箭中即「瞄准」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fourteenth century, and the noun followed soon after.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个动词，名词紧随其后出现。

items.en: The figurative sense 'to intend' is recorded in the sixteenth century, first in letters and essays.
items.cn: 「意图、打算」的比喻义在十六世纪有记录，最早见于书信与随笔。

items.en: The noun settled into the sense 'purpose', and the phrase with the aim of became standard in reports.
items.cn: 名词固定为「目的」义，with the aim of 成为报告中的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on aim; the near-meaning group gathers goals and targets, from the concrete to the abstract.
note.cn: 形近组收由 aim 构成的一族词；近义组收目标类词，从具体到抽象。

entries.definition: Having no clear purpose or direction.
entries.definitionCN: 没有明确目的或方向的。

entries.definition: Without a purpose, in a wandering way.
entries.definitionCN: 漫无目的地，四处游荡地。

entries.definition: The state of having no aim.
entries.definitionCN: 没有目标的状态。

entries.definition: A physical object shot at, or a result one plans to reach.
entries.definitionCN: 被射击的实物，或计划达到的结果。

entries.definition: The result that a person or plan is trying to achieve.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或计划努力要达到的结果。

entries.definition: The reason for which something is done, rather than the result itself.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的原因，而非结果本身。

normalIntro.en: Two real layers carry the word: the Latin verb aestimare, 'to estimate', and its French descendant aesmer.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实层次承载这个词：拉丁动词 aestimare「估量」，以及它的法语后裔 aesmer。

normal.en: Aim and estimate are cousins: you must judge the distance before you let the arrow go.
normal.cn: aim 与 estimate 是表亲：松手之前必须先估准距离。

normal.en: Aim at a thing, aim for a result: at hits the object, for reaches the number.
normal.cn: aim at 后面是物体，aim for 后面是数值：一个打中东西，一个够到数字。

normal.en: Take aim is the moment before release, when everything is still.
normal.cn: take aim 是松手前的那一瞬，一切都静止着。

normal.en: Add -less and the arrow has no target: aimless.
normal.cn: 加上 -less，箭就没有靶子：aimless。

normal.en: Three letters, one syllable, long vowel: aim rhymes with name.
normal.cn: 三个字母、一个音节、长元音：aim 与 name 押韵。

abstract.en: Every aim contains a judgement: to point at something is to have already measured it.
abstract.cn: 每一个瞄准都包含一次判断：能指向某物，说明已经量过它。

abstract.en: The word slides from arrows to plans because intention is aiming without a weapon.
abstract.cn: 这个词从箭矢滑向计划，因为意图就是不带武器的瞄准。

abstract.en: A nation with aims sounds purposeful, but the same word used of a joke becomes a threat.
abstract.cn: 国家有 aims 听起来很有目标感，可同一个词用在玩笑上就变成了威胁。

examples.en: She aimed the camera at the bird.
examples.cn: 她把相机对准了那只鸟。

examples.en: The campaign aims to cut waste by half.
examples.cn: 这场运动旨在把浪费减少一半。

examples.en: The joke was aimed at the new intern.
examples.cn: 那个玩笑是针对新来的实习生的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶姆」——诶，姆指一竖，对准靶心。

root: 源自古法语 aesmer「估量、瞄准」，其前身为拉丁语 aestimare「估价、判断」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses keep the picture of a mark being pointed at: a physical target, a planned result, a stated purpose, or a person on the receiving end.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都保留「对准某个点」的画面：实物靶子、计划中的结果、说出的目的，或被针对的那个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowstring drawn back, the arrowhead fixed on a single distant point.
core.cn: 核心意象：弓弦拉满，箭尖锁定远处唯一的一点。

branches.en: a lens turned until the bird is sharp
branches.cn: 转动到鸟变清晰的那只镜头

branches.en: a plan with a number written at the end
branches.cn: 末尾写着一个数字的计划

branches.en: a sentence beginning with our aim is
branches.cn: 以 our aim is 开头的那句话

branches.en: a remark that lands on one person in the room
branches.cn: 恰好落在屋里某一个人身上的那句话

branches.en: one pointed intention, in the field and in the office
branches.cn: 同一个指向前方的意图，一在野外，一在办公室

intro.en: A Latin verb of estimating, its French descendant, and the negative endings built on aim.
intro.cn: 一个表示「估量」的拉丁动词、它的法语后裔，以及建在 aim 上的否定词尾。

latinIntro.en: aestimare is recorded Latin; aesmer is Old French, and the English word comes from the French form.
latinIntro.cn: aestimare 是有文献记录的拉丁词；aesmer 是古法语，英语词来自法语形式。

items.meaning: the state of having no aim

definition_zh: 空气；空中；神态；播出；表达（意见）
definition_en: the mixture of gases we breathe, the space above the ground, a manner or impression, or to broadcast something
core_image: 推开窗，一股看不见的气流涌进来，窗帘被轻轻抬起
scene: 清晨推开木窗，山谷里的雾气正慢慢散开。The mountain air was cold and sharp.
sceneCN: 这里 air 是「空气」（第 1 个义项：我们呼吸的气体混合物）；句意为山里的空气又冷又清冽。图中可辨识物件：木窗、雾气、山谷。

pos.zh: 名词：空气；空中；神态；气氛
动词：播出；晾晒；表达（意见）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「通风的；轻快的」
由本词加否定后缀构成，义为「不通风的；没有空气的」
由 airy 加副词后缀构成，义为「轻飘飘地；漫不经心地」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「晾晒；播出；公开讨论」

senses.title: The gas we breathe
senses.definition: the invisible mixture of gases that surrounds the earth and that people and animals breathe
senses.definitionCN: 包围地球、供人与动物呼吸的看不见的气体混合物
senses.example: The mountain air was cold and sharp.
senses.exampleCN: 山里的空气又冷又清冽。
senses.why: This is the word's oldest layer, from Greek and Latin words for the lower atmosphere; everything else in English grew out of it by metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层，来自希腊语与拉丁语中表示下层大气的词；英语里的其他义项都是由此比喻而来。

senses.title: The space above the ground
senses.definition: the open space above the ground, especially as the place where aircraft travel
senses.definitionCN: 地面上方的开阔空间，尤指飞行器往来的空间
senses.example: The rescue team moved the supplies by air.
senses.exampleCN: 救援队通过空运把物资送了过去。
senses.why: Since we move through air when we fly, the substance became the medium of travel, giving phrases such as by air and air travel.
senses.whyCN: 因为飞行时是在空气中穿行，这种物质便成了交通的媒介，于是有 by air、air travel 这类说法。

senses.title: A manner or impression
senses.definition: the impression a person or place gives through appearance or manner
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一个地方通过外表、举止给人的印象
senses.example: She answered with an air of confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着一种自信的神态回答。
senses.why: Something as invisible as air can still be felt in a room, so the word came to name an atmosphere that cannot be pointed to.
senses.whyCN: 像空气这样看不见的东西在屋里仍能被感觉到，于是这个词用来指那种指不出来的气氛。

senses.title: To broadcast
senses.definition: to send out a programme on radio, television, or the internet
senses.definitionCN: 通过广播、电视或网络播放节目
senses.example: The interview will air on Sunday evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这段访谈将在周日晚上播出。
senses.why: Radio waves travel through the air, so putting a programme 'on the air' became simply to air it.
senses.whyCN: 无线电波通过空气传播，于是把节目「送上电波」就简化为 air 这个动词。

senses.title: To express an opinion publicly
senses.definition: to make an opinion, complaint, or grievance known in public
senses.definitionCN: 把意见、不满或委屈公开说出来
senses.example: Residents used the meeting to air their complaints about noise.
senses.exampleCN: 居民利用这次会议说出了他们对噪音的不满。
senses.why: Bringing a hidden thing into the open is like letting stale air out of a room, which is why airing a grievance means making it public.
senses.whyCN: 把藏着的东西拿到明处，就像给屋子放掉浊气，所以 air a grievance 就是把不满公开。

intro.en: Air travelled from Greek to Latin to French before English took it, and along the way it picked up the senses of sky, manner, and broadcast.
intro.cn: air 从希腊语经拉丁语、法语进入英语，一路带上了天空、神态与播出这些义项。

items.en: Aer meant the lower, misty layer of the atmosphere, as opposed to the bright upper ether.
items.cn: aēr 指大气中较低、带雾气的一层，与上层明亮的以太相对。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as aer, keeping both the 'air' and the 'mist' associations.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊词作 aer，同时保留「空气」与「雾气」两重联想。

items.en: Old French air added the sense of a person's bearing or appearance, which English inherited.
items.cn: 古法语 air 增加了「人的举止、外表」这一义，英语继承了下来。

items.en: English records air in the thirteenth century for the element, and soon after for demeanour and for melody.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪记录 air 指空气，不久后也指神态与曲调。

items.en: Broadcasting gave the verb its modern sense, first on the air and then simply to air a programme.
items.cn: 广播给了动词现代义：先有 on the air，后来直接说 air a programme。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on air; the near-meaning group gathers the sky, the atmosphere and a person's manner.
note.cn: 形近组收由 air 构成的词；近义组收天空、大气与人的仪态。

entries.definition: Full of fresh air, or light and casual in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 通风良好的，或举止轻快随意的。

entries.definition: Having no fresh air, stuffy.
entries.definitionCN: 没有新鲜空气的；闷的。

entries.definition: The act of drying something in the air, or of broadcasting it.
entries.definitionCN: 晾晒，或播出的行为。

entries.definition: The whole envelope of gases round a planet, or the mood of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕行星的整层气体，或一个地方的气氛。

entries.definition: A gentle wind, air that is actually moving.
entries.definitionCN: 轻风，真正流动起来的空气。

entries.definition: The way a person behaves or carries themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的举止或姿态。

normalIntro.en: Two real layers carry the word: Greek aer and its Latin and French descendants.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实层次承载这个词：希腊语 aēr 及其拉丁语、法语后裔。

normal.en: Air is what you cannot see but still feel when a window opens.
normal.cn: air 是你看不见、但一开窗就能感觉到的东西。

normal.en: On the air means broadcasting, because the signal travels through the air.
normal.cn: on the air 意为「正在播出」，因为信号正是通过空气传播的。

normal.en: An air of confidence is confidence you can sense but not point to.
normal.cn: an air of confidence 是能感觉到、却指不出来的那种自信。

normal.en: Air is uncountable for the gas, but airs means affectations: she puts on airs.
normal.cn: 指气体时 air 不可数，但 airs 指做作的姿态：she puts on airs。

normal.en: The verb is regular: aired, airing, no doubling of the r.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：aired、airing，r 不加倍。

abstract.en: Air is the cheapest thing we share, which is why polluting it is a problem nobody owns alone.
abstract.cn: 空气是我们共享的最廉价之物，所以污染它成了一个谁也无法独自负责的问题。

abstract.en: The same word covers weather and manners because both are felt rather than held.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指天气又指举止，因为两者都是被感觉到、而不是被握住的东西。

abstract.en: To air a complaint is to let pressure escape: speech works like a valve.
abstract.cn: 把不满说出来就像放掉压力：言语在这里起的是阀门的作用。

examples.en: The mountain air was cold and sharp.
examples.cn: 山里的空气又冷又清冽。

examples.en: She answered with an air of confidence.
examples.cn: 她带着一种自信的神态回答。

examples.en: The interview will air on Sunday evening.
examples.cn: 这段访谈将在周日晚上播出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶尔」——诶，尔后一阵风过来，满屋子都是新鲜空气。

root: 源自希腊语 aēr「下层大气、雾气」，经拉丁语 aer 与古法语 air 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One invisible medium runs through all five senses: the gas itself, the space it fills, the mood it carries, the waves that broadcast through it, and the relief of letting it out.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项贯穿着同一种看不见的介质：气体本身、它占据的空间、它承载的气氛、通过它传播的电波，以及把它放出去时的痛快。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a window opens, and an invisible current lifts the curtain.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗子一开，一股看不见的气流把窗帘抬起。

branches.en: cold air rushing into a warm room
branches.cn: 涌进暖屋的一股冷气

branches.en: a crate lowered by parachute
branches.cn: 用降落伞空投下去的箱子

branches.en: a speaker whose calm fills the hall
branches.cn: 让整个大厅安静下来的那种从容

branches.en: a red light above a studio door
branches.cn: 演播室门上亮起的红灯

branches.en: a complaint finally said aloud
branches.cn: 终于被大声说出口的抱怨

intro.en: A Greek noun for the lower atmosphere, its Latin and French forms, and the English endings built on it.
intro.cn: 一个表示下层大气的希腊名词、它的拉丁语与法语形式，以及建在其上的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek aer and Latin aer are recorded; the further origin of the Greek word is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 aēr 与拉丁语 aer 都有文献记录，希腊词的更早来源不确定。

items.meaning: of the air, or an antenna

definition_zh: 航空器；飞机；（军事）空中力量
definition_en: any machine or vehicle that can fly, such as a plane, helicopter, or balloon
core_image: 跑道尽头，一只金属的鸟离开地面，把影子留在下面
scene: 航母甲板上，地勤人员打着手势引导一架灰色飞机就位。The carrier can launch aircraft every thirty seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 aircraft 是「航空器、飞机」（第 1 个义项：能在空中飞行的机械装置）；句意为这艘航母每三十秒就能弹射一架飞机。图中可辨识物件：甲板、手势、起落架。

pos.zh: 名词：航空器；飞机（单复数同形）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表人成分构成，义为「空军士兵」
由本词与 carrier 合成的名词，义为「航空母舰」

senses.title: Any flying machine
senses.definition: any machine or vehicle designed to fly, including planes, helicopters, and balloons
senses.definitionCN: 任何为飞行而设计的机械或载具，包括飞机、直升机与气球
senses.example: The carrier can launch aircraft every thirty seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘航母每三十秒就能弹射一架飞机。
senses.why: The compound joined air and craft, where craft meant a vessel, so the word names a vessel whose element is air rather than water.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把 air 与 craft 结合，而 craft 本指船只，所以它命名的是以空气而非水为活动场所的载具。

senses.title: Hostile planes as a force
senses.definition: in military use, flying machines considered collectively as a threat or force, as in enemy aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 军事用语中把飞行器作为整体来看的威胁或力量，如 enemy aircraft
senses.example: Radar reported enemy aircraft approaching from the north.
senses.exampleCN: 雷达报告有敌机从北方接近。
senses.why: Military reports count aircraft as a mass, so the unchanged plural and the collective use together make it a force rather than a list of machines.
senses.whyCN: 军事报告把航空器当作一个整体来计数，单复数同形与集合用法共同让它成为一种力量，而不是一架架机器的清单。

intro.en: Aircraft is a modern English compound: the element air plus craft, an old word for a vessel or a skill.
intro.cn: aircraft 是近代英语复合词：air 加上 craft，而 craft 原本指船只或技艺。

items.en: Craeft meant 'power, skill, a trade', and by extension a vessel built with skill.
items.cn: cræft 意为「力量、技艺、行业」，并引申为凭技艺造出的器具。

items.en: Craft was already used for boats, giving watercraft and later the pattern for other vehicles.
items.cn: craft 早已用来指船，产生 watercraft，并为其他载具的说法提供范式。

items.en: Ballooning and early flight produced compounds such as aircraft, formed on the model of watercraft.
items.cn: 气球飞行与早期航空产生了 aircraft 这类复合词，是照着 watercraft 的模式造的。

items.en: With powered flight the word became the general term, covering planes, helicopters and drones.
items.cn: 随着动力飞行出现，这个词成为统称，涵盖飞机、直升机与无人机。

items.en: The plural stays aircraft, a trace of the old mass-noun use of craft.
items.cn: 复数仍作 aircraft，这是 craft 旧有集合名词用法留下的痕迹。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other -craft vehicles; the near-meaning group gathers specific kinds of flying machine.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 -craft 结尾的载具；近义组收具体的飞行器种类。

entries.definition: A vehicle designed to travel in space.
entries.definitionCN: 为在太空中航行而设计的载具。

entries.definition: A vehicle that rides on a cushion of air over water or land.
entries.definitionCN: 靠气垫在水面或地面上行驶的载具。

entries.definition: A boat or ship, or such vessels collectively.
entries.definitionCN: 船艇，或这类船只的总称。

entries.definition: A powered flying vehicle with fixed wings, the American term.
entries.definitionCN: 有固定机翼的动力飞行器，美式说法。

entries.definition: A flying machine lifted by rotating blades.
entries.definitionCN: 靠旋转桨叶升空的飞行器。

entries.definition: An aircraft that flies without an engine, riding rising air.
entries.definitionCN: 没有发动机、借上升气流飞行的航空器。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: air and craft, an old word for a vessel.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：air 与表示船只的古老词 craft。

normal.en: Watercraft sails on water; aircraft flies through air: the second element stays the same.
normal.cn: watercraft 在水上走，aircraft 在空气中飞：后一个部件不变。

normal.en: Craft is both singular and plural, so one aircraft and two aircraft are spelled alike.
normal.cn: craft 单复数同形，所以 one aircraft 与 two aircraft 拼写一样。

normal.en: The stress falls on air: AIR-craft.
normal.cn: 重音落在 air 上：AIR-craft。

normal.en: An aircraft carrier is a ship that carries the very thing it is named after.
normal.cn: aircraft carrier 是一条船，专门载着与它名字同源的那个东西。

normal.en: Do not write aircaft: keep the r of air and the f of craft.
normal.cn: 不要写成 aircaft：air 的 r 与 craft 的 f 都要留住。

abstract.en: Aircraft names a machine by the element it moves through, the way watercraft names one by water.
abstract.cn: aircraft 用所穿行的介质来命名机器，就像 watercraft 用水来命名。

abstract.en: The unchanged plural treats flying machines as a mass, which is exactly how radar sees them.
abstract.cn: 单复数同形把飞行器看成一团整体，而这正是雷达看它们的方式。

abstract.en: The word is a small record of how English builds new technology out of old words for boats.
abstract.cn: 这个词小小地记录了英语如何用「船」的旧词来造新技术之名。

examples.en: The carrier can launch aircraft every thirty seconds.
examples.cn: 这艘航母每三十秒就能弹射一架飞机。

examples.en: Radar reported enemy aircraft approaching from the north.
examples.cn: 雷达报告有敌机从北方接近。

examples.en: The museum displays several early aircraft made of wood and cloth.
examples.cn: 博物馆陈列着几架木布结构的早期飞机。

definition_en: a company that operates regular flights for passengers or cargo

scene: 登机口上方的屏幕上滚动着目的地，队伍排得很长。The airline offered vouchers to passengers whose flight was cancelled.

pos.zh: 名词：航空公司；航线
